stem: A client taking digoxin is found to have hypercalcemia. Why is this finding clinically important?

options.A: Hypercalcemia predisposes the client to digitalis toxicity
options.C: Hypercalcemia makes digoxin ineffective in the same way as hypocalcemia
options.D: Serum calcium has no clinically relevant relationship to digoxin toxicity

rationale: The digoxin prescribing information states that hypercalcemia from any cause predisposes a patient to digitalis toxicity and that rapidly administered calcium may produce serious arrhythmias in digitalized patients.
educational_objective: Recognize hypercalcemia as a factor that predisposes a client receiving digoxin to toxicity.
source_locator: Precautions > Use in Patients with Electrolyte Disorders
source_claim_supported: Hypercalcemia predisposes a patient to digitalis toxicity.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16
correction_summary: Removed the more speculative “increased myocardial sensitivity” wording and used the label’s exact toxicity statement.
audit_findings: A is verbatim in meaning from the label. B and D directly contradict it; C incorrectly transfers the label’s hypocalcemia statement to hypercalcemia. No second answer remains.
audit_reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol Rule 1 — final semantic audit
